authority: AgriN Regenerative Agronomy Knowledge Base (ICAR / CRIDA / FAO Aligned)

practices.name: Legume-Inclusive Crop Rotation
practices.description: Systematic succession of deep-rooted legumes (e.g., Chickpea, Pigeonpea, Green Gram) alternating with exhaustive cereal crops (Wheat, Maize, Sorghum) to break weed/pest cycles and replenish soil nitrogen.
expected_benefits: Biological nitrogen fixation (30-60 kg N/ha equivalent)
Breaks soil-borne pathogen cycles and root nematode pressure
Improves sub-soil porosity and water infiltration
potential_tradeoffs: Requires market access or farm storage for secondary pulse crops
Short-term gross revenue might differ from mono-cropping cash crops
practices.source_reference: ICAR-Indian Institute of Farming Systems Research (IIFSR) Long-Term Crop Rotation Trials

practices.name: Multi-Species Cover Cropping
practices.description: Planting fast-growing herbaceous vegetative cover (e.g., Sunnhemp / Crotalaria juncea, Dhaincha / Sesbania bispinosa, Cowpea) during fallow intervals to prevent erosion and suppress weeds.
expected_benefits: Adds 15-25 tonnes/ha fresh biomass for green manuring
Reduces topsoil erosion during intense onset monsoons by up to 70%
Feeds mycorrhizal fungi and beneficial soil microbiota
potential_tradeoffs: Consumes residual soil moisture if terminated late in dryland systems
Requires seed availability and timely termination equipment
practices.source_reference: CRIDA (Central Research Institute for Dryland Agriculture) Green Manuring Protocols

practices.name: Strip Intercropping & Canopy Stratification
practices.description: Growing two or more crops simultaneously in proximity (e.g., Pigeonpea + Soybean in 1:4 ratio, or Maize + Cowpea) to maximize land equivalent ratio (LER) and photosynthetic canopy capture.
expected_benefits: Land Equivalent Ratio (LER) typically between 1.25 and 1.45
Insurance against total crop failure under erratic monsoon rainfall
Micro-climate moderation reducing evapotranspiration
potential_tradeoffs: Mechanical harvesting is more complex compared to sole cropping
Inter-species light competition if planting geometry is misaligned
practices.source_reference: ICRISAT / ICAR Intercropping Benchmarks for Rainfed Semi-Arid Tropics

practices.name: Conservation / Minimum Tillage
practices.description: Minimizing mechanical soil disturbance and leaving at least 30% crop residue cover on the soil surface, preserving fungal hyphae networks and soil aggregate stability.
expected_benefits: Reduces tractor diesel consumption by 40-60 liters/ha
Maintains stable soil macro-aggregates and macro-pores
Decreases soil carbon oxidation loss
potential_tradeoffs: May require specialized direct-seed drill (e.g., Happy Seeder / Super Seeder)
Early-stage perennial weed management requires careful attention
practices.source_reference: Borlaug Institute for South Asia (BISA) Conservation Agriculture Studies

practices.name: In-Situ Crop Residue Retention & Mulching
practices.description: Retention of crop stubble, straw, and harvest residues on the field rather than burning or removing, creating a protective mulch blanket.
expected_benefits: Lowers peak summer soil temperature by 4°C to 8°C
Reduces surface evaporation, conserving 15-25% irrigation water
Eliminates particulate smog from open field burning
potential_tradeoffs: Risk of harboring insect pests (e.g., stem borers) if residue is not managed properly
Slow decomposition in arid conditions without adequate microbial moisture
practices.source_reference: National Academy of Agricultural Sciences (NAAS) Residue Management Directives

practices.name: Integrated Nutrient Management (INM)
practices.description: Synergistic combination of organic manures (FYM, vermicompost, biochar), biofertilizers (Rhizobium, Azotobacter, PSB), and precision synthetic fertilizers based on soil test card deficits.
expected_benefits: Improves nutrient use efficiency (NUE) by 20-35%
Gradually restores active fraction of soil organic carbon
Supplies essential secondary and micronutrients (S, Zn, Fe, B)
potential_tradeoffs: Bulkiness of farmyard manure requires transport logistics
Quality standardization of commercial compost and bio-inoculants varies
practices.source_reference: ICAR-Indian Institute of Soil Science (IISS) INM Guidelines

practices.name: Micro-Irrigation & Broad Bed Furrow (BBF)
practices.description: Combining land configuration (Broad Bed Furrow or Ridge & Furrow) with drip/micro-sprinkler systems to manage excess drainage in monsoons and conserve moisture during dry spells.
expected_benefits: Water savings of 30-50% compared to conventional flood irrigation
Prevents root waterlogging in heavy Vertisols during cloudburst events
Enhances crop yield by 15-25% via uniform aeration
potential_tradeoffs: Initial capital expenditure for drip lines and filters (partially offset by PMKSY subsidy)
Requires maintenance to prevent emitter clogging from hard water salts
practices.source_reference: CRIDA / VNMKV Broad Bed Furrow Technology Validation for Rainfed Vertisols

practices.name: Ecological & Integrated Pest Management (IPM)
practices.description: Biological control utilizing pheromone traps, yellow sticky traps, border trap crops (Marigold in Cotton/Tomato), Trichoderma, and parasitoids to keep pest populations below Economic Injury Level (EIL).
expected_benefits: Reduces toxic chemical pesticide sprays by 50-80%
Prevents secondary pest resurgence and pesticide resistance
Protects native honeybees and beneficial pollinator populations
potential_tradeoffs: Requires routine field scouting rather than calendar-based spraying
Biological agents have narrower environmental windows than broad-spectrum chemicals
practices.source_reference: ICAR-National Research Centre for Integrated Pest Management (NCIPM)

practices.name: Agroforestry & Field Bund Plantation
practices.description: Integrating multipurpose perennial trees (Subabul / Leucaena, Neem, Moringa, Gliricidia) along farm boundaries or windbreaks to provide leaf fodder, microclimate moderation, and deep nutrient pumping.
expected_benefits: Long-term biological carbon sequestration in tree woody biomass
Windbreak effect reducing mechanical crop lodging and desiccating winds
Supplementary farmer income from pruned timber, fruit, or high-protein fodder
potential_tradeoffs: Can cause border shading on adjacent row crops if canopies are not pollarded
Multi-year gestation period before tree economic benefits realize
practices.source_reference: Central Agroforestry Research Institute (CAFRI) Bund Agroforestry Systems

practices.name: Biochar & Stable Carbon Pyrolysis Amendment
practices.description: Application of pyrolyzed farm bio-residues (cotton stalks, pigeonpea stalks) converted into stable porous recalcitrant black carbon to permanently augment soil water holding capacity and cation exchange.
expected_benefits: High persistence carbon sequestered with hundreds of years half-life
Boosts soil water retention in sandy or degraded soils by 15-30%
Reduces nutrient leaching in high-rainfall zones
potential_tradeoffs: Requires on-farm low-emission pyrolysis kiln or centralized biochar producer
Must be co-composted with manure/urine prior to application to avoid initial nitrogen draw-down
practices.source_reference: CRIDA / ICAR-IISS Biochar Field Application Assessments
